data.title: Chinese Shoppers Are Joining Membership Clubs. Walmart Is Winning. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Tanner Brown

China's shoppers have found an unusual way to get their money's worth: paying a supermarket for permission to shop.

An annual membership at Walmart's Sam's Club costs 260 yuan, about $37. The chain had 10.7 million paying members in China as of June, and its brisk expansion looks almost out of place in an economy whose consumers have grown increasingly reluctant to open their wallets.

Elsewhere, the numbers are grim. Sales at stores devoted to a single brand fell 10.3% in the first nine months of 2026, while department-store sales declined 2.9%, according to government figures released Monday. Supermarkets and convenience stores managed gains of 4.1% and 5.2%, respectively.

Warehouse membership stores, meanwhile, posted growth exceeding 25% through August, according to the China National Commercial Information Center. Overall Chinese retail sales rose just 1.1% in the first nine months.

The figures don't prove that shoppers have abandoned famous labels. A pair of sneakers bought online doesn't ring up at a brand-exclusive store. But they suggest that where Chinese consumers shop — and whom they trust to deliver value — is changing.

Consider Walmart and Nike. Walmart's China revenue rose 20.7% in its latest reported quarter, to $7 billion, excluding currency fluctuations. New clubs helped, but comparable sales, which strip out much of the effect of expansion, also climbed 9.7%. E-commerce sales jumped 26% and accounted for 55% of China sales. Sam's Club was a major contributor.

Nike is heading the opposite direction. Its Greater China revenue plunged 26% in its latest quarter on a currency-neutral basis, its ninth consecutive quarterly decline there. Digital sales through its own channels fell 28%, and its physical-store sales dropped 14%.

Yet Nike's troubles aren't universal. Rival Adidas reported a 15% increase in Greater China sales in its second quarter, also excluding currency fluctuations. China's Anta Sports grew first-half revenue 12.9% across its global portfolio of brands. Chinese shoppers clearly haven't stopped buying sportswear. They're becoming more selective about which brands get their money.

Nike is trying to respond. Beginning in January, the company plans to concentrate Chinese online sales in official storefronts and its own channels, phasing out most partner-operated shops.

"When the experience is consistent, the brand becomes stronger," Cathy Sparks, Nike's Greater China chief, wrote in a post on the company's website.

The comparison between Nike and Walmart has limits: One sells discretionary apparel, the other plenty of groceries and household essentials. The lesson isn't that supermarkets have discovered a cure for weak spending. It's that brand recognition alone is no guarantee of growth.

For years, international companies could charge hefty premiums in China through name recognition, celebrity endorsements and prestigious storefronts. After a prolonged property slump and years of shaky consumer confidence, shoppers have more reason to ask what those premiums actually buy.

Consumer-market analyst Tang Jiansheng pointed to down jackets sold at Sam's Club and other supermarkets as evidence of changing attitudes toward labels and quality. He cited a 499-yuan Sam's Club jacket that sold out at multiple stores.

"Consumers are no longer buying a particular clothing brand, but the retailer's ability to select products and its promise of quality," he said.

That's Sam's pitch: a limited assortment of products it has already vetted, including private-label groceries and household goods, alongside competitive prices and speedy delivery. Customers pay for the idea that somebody has done the comparison shopping for them. Once they have paid, they have another reason to return.

In an October survey by Chinese research firm iiMedia, 51.2% of respondents cited access to carefully selected merchandise as a reason to shop at warehouse clubs. That helps explain the appeal of Costco, too. Its private-label products invite shoppers to trust the retailer's judgment rather than a manufacturer's logo.

But trust is expensive to maintain. In June, China's market regulator summoned Walmart executives over recurring food-safety problems at Sam's Club. Rapid expansion has placed new demands on a business built around screening its suppliers and products.

Yuan Shuai, an analyst with Zhongjing Media Think Tank, argues that the membership model relies on confidence in product quality. "Once that foundation of trust is shaken, even the fastest expansion is just a castle in the air," he said.

For investors, the winners won't necessarily be the cheapest retailers or the companies with the flashiest names. Walmart's China growth also comes with the costs of opening clubs, making deliveries and keeping prices attractive. Strong sales aren't the same as strong profits.

The irony is that Walmart may be winning China's contest for consumer loyalty by asking shoppers to pay for it in advance.

data.title: BioInvent's BI-1808 and KEYTRUDA® Induce Durable Responses in Heavily Pretreated Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer
data.description:
Updated efficacy data in 34 evaluable patients with a chemotherapy-free regimen; randomized Part C will add BI-1808 to the new standard of care

  • 24% objective response rate (8 of 34 evaluable patients: 1 complete and 7 partial responses), including patients with high-grade serous and clear cell carcinoma
  • 53% disease control rate, with several patients in stable disease beyond 10 months; 6 patients were still on treatment at data cutoff
  • Median progression-free survival of 4.1 months per RECIST, compared with 2.1 months reported for pembrolizumab alone1 (indirect comparison); 10.3 months per iRECIST
  • Duration of response was not met at cutoff (median follow-up 11.6 months), suggesting that responses are durable
  • Well tolerated: fewer than 5% treatment-related discontinuations among 81 solid tumor patients treated with the combination
  • Part C will add BI-1808 to pembrolizumab plus weekly paclitaxel ± bevacizumab in a randomized design; first data expected in H2 2027

Lund, Sweden – October 24, 2026 – BioInvent International AB (“BioInvent”) (Nasdaq Stockholm: BINV), a leader in the discovery of novel immune-modulatory antibodies, today announced updated data from Part B of its ongoing clinical study of BI-1808, a first-in-class anti-TNFR2 antibody, combined with MSD’s (Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, USA) anti-PD-1 therapy KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) in patients with advanced platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer (PRROC) and a median of four prior lines of therapy.

The data are presented today in poster #2009P (12:00–12:45 CEST) at the ESMO Congress 2026 in Madrid. They update the 25-patient analysis reported at ASCO 2026, the ESMO abstract published on October 19 and now include 34 evaluable patients (cutoff September 14, 2026).

Checkpoint inhibitors alone have limited activity in PRROC because CD8+ T cells poorly infiltrate the tumor microenvironment, where immunosuppressive TNFR2-expressing cells such as regulatory T cells (Tregs) and tumor-associated myeloid cells are enriched and further suppress antitumor T-cell activity. BI-1808 is a ligand-blocking, FcγR-engaging TNFR2 antibody designed to deplete these Tregs and remodel the myeloid compartment, promoting activation, expansion and infiltration of anti-tumoral CD8+ T cells.

“Patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer have few therapeutic options, and checkpoint inhibitors alone have done little to change that,” said Martin Welschof, Chief Executive Officer at BioInvent. “With Part B complete, a 24% response rate and durable disease control in heavily pretreated patients suggest that targeting TNFR2 can add significant activity when combined with immune checkpoint inhibition. Our next step will be to evaluate BI-1808 as an add-on to the newly established pembrolizumab and paclitaxel backbone in a randomized Part C.”

Durable responses in heavily pretreated patients

The 34 evaluable patients (of 40 planned) had a median age of 62 years and had received a median of four prior lines of therapy; 88% had received three or more, and all had received platinum. Histology was high-grade serous adenocarcinoma (HGSA) in 59% and clear cell in 41%, and 24% had liver involvement at screening. They were treated with BI-1808 1000 mg plus pembrolizumab 200 mg every three weeks for up to two years.

  • Responses were seen in both HGSA and clear cell ovarian cancer, including in patients with active liver metastases.
  • In some patients, tumors grew before shrinking. This may reflect pseudoprogression (an apparent increase in size caused by immune cells entering the tumor) or a delay in CD8+ T-cell expansion, an observation previously made in preclinical models (ASCO#2605 poster).
  • Most cases of progressive disease were not confirmed on a follow-up scan. These patients left the study with unconfirmed progressive disease under iRECIST, which explains the difference between PFS and iPFS.

What is iRECIST? iRECIST is an adaptation of the standard RECIST criteria for immunotherapies. It requires confirmation of progression before treatment is stopped, so it can capture responses that appear after initial apparent tumor growth. Median PFS by iRECIST may therefore be longer than by RECIST.

In KEYNOTE-100, pembrolizumab alone produced an objective response rate of 8% and a disease control rate of 37%. Median progression-free survival was 2.1 months by RECIST 1.1, and no iRECIST-based figure was reported.

Well tolerated, with fewer than 5% treatment-related discontinuations

  • 81 patients with solid tumors have received BI-1808 plus pembrolizumab to date
  • Immune-related adverse events were manageable, and the rate of Grade 3 or higher adverse events was low
  • Treatment-related discontinuations in the combination arm occurred in 4 patients (fewer than 5%)

Immune data consistent with the mechanism of BI-1808

  • Reduced Tregs in the blood of ovarian cancer patients, and a shift in the CD8+ T-cell over Treg ratio in tumor biopsies
  • Induction of IL-12 and CXCL10, cytokines associated with myeloid reprogramming, proinflammatory activation, and effector T cell recruitment
  • Induction of CCL19 and CXCL13, chemokines associated with tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) formation
  • Proinflammatory myeloid and TLS-stimulating cytokines were strongly potentiated when BI-1808 was combined with pembrolizumab2

Next step: adding BI-1808 to pembrolizumab and paclitaxel

The KEYNOTE-B96 study3 recently added an immunotherapy option to the standard weekly paclitaxel ± bevacizumab regimen in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, improving median PFS (8.3 vs 7.2 months) and overall survival (17.7 vs 14.0 months) versus chemotherapy alone. This creates a backbone on which to test additional mechanisms.

In a mouse model of ovarian cancer (ID8), the combination of a BI-1808 surrogate antibody, paclitaxel and anti-PD-1 improved survival, with increases in serum cytokines indicating myeloid reprogramming and TLS formation.

Part C of the study will randomize 20 patients to each of three arms: BI-1808 1000 mg, BI-1808 500 mg, or control, each with pembrolizumab and weekly paclitaxel +/- bevacizumab. Part C is expected to start in Q1 2027, with first data in H2 2027, subject to enrollment.

Poster details

Title: From Modest to Meaningful: Targeting TNFR2 with BI-1808 to Unlock Checkpoint Inhibitor Efficacy in Platinum-Resistant Recurrent Ovarian Cancer (PRROC)

Poster number: 2009P | Session: Investigational immunotherapy

Date and time: October 24, 12:00–12:45 CEST

First author: Rebecca Kristeleit, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, United Kingdom

The poster will be available on the publications tab of the BioInvent website: https://www.bioinvent.com/en/our-science/scientific-publications

About the trial

The BI-1808 study (NCT04752826, KEYNOTE-D20) is an ongoing open-label Phase 1/2a study evaluating BI-1808 as a single agent (Part A), in combination with pembrolizumab (Part B) and in combination with pembrolizumab and paclitaxel ± bevacizumab (Part C). Patients were enrolled at 14 study locations in Europe and the United States.

Clinical trial collaboration and supply agreement

KEYTRUDA® is a registered trademark of Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC, a subsidiary of Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, USA. Since August 2021, BioInvent has a clinical trial collaboration and supply agreement with MSD, a tradename of Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, USA, to evaluate the combination of BI-1808 and MSD’s anti-PD-1 therapy KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab).

About ovarian cancer

Ovarian cancer is a serious and life-threatening disease, affecting more than 320,000 women worldwide each year.4 It is frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage because its symptoms are often difficult to recognize, and is the eighth most common cancer and the eighth leading cause of cancer-related death among women globally.5 Recurrence affects an estimated 70–90% of patients with advanced disease after initial treatment.6 Five-year survival rate is estimated at 50%, across all stages, types and regions.7,8

About BI-1808

BI-1808 is a first-in-class drug candidate targeting TNFR2, which is upregulated on both immunosuppressive and inflammatory tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and on myeloid cells in the tumor microenvironment. BI-1808 is in clinical development for T-cell lymphoma and solid tumors, and has shown single-agent activity and excellent tolerability, and efficacy and a favorable safety profile in combination with pembrolizumab.

BI-1808 has received FDA Fast Track Designation for the treatment of ovarian cancer and for relapsed or refractory mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome, FDA Orphan Drug Designation for T-cell lymphoma, and Orphan Drug Designation in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma from the European Medicines Agency.

About BioInvent

BioInvent International AB (Nasdaq Stockholm: BINV) is a clinical-stage biotech company that discovers and develops novel and first-in-class immuno-modulatory antibodies for cancer therapy, with drug candidates in ongoing clinical programs in Phase 1/2 trials for the treatment of solid tumors and hematological cancer. The Company’s validated, proprietary F.I.R.S.T™ technology platform identifies both targets and the antibodies that bind to them, generating many promising new immune-modulatory candidates to fuel the Company’s own clinical development pipeline and providing licensing and partnering opportunities.

The Company generates revenues from research collaborations and license agreements with multiple top-tier pharmaceutical companies, as well as from producing antibodies for third parties in the Company’s fully integrated manufacturing unit. More information is available at www.bioinvent.com.

data.title: EAAA India Alternatives secures ₹360 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
data.description:
EAAA India Alternatives Ltd, an arm of Edelweiss Financial Services, has raised around ₹360 crore from anchor investors ahead of its ₹1,200-crore initial public offering (IPO), which opens for subscription on October 26.

The company allocated 21,62,161 equity shares to anchor investors at ₹1,665 apiece, the upper end of the price band, according to circulars uploaded with exchanges.

The anchor book saw participation from 10 mutual funds, including HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, Nippon India Mutual Fund and Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund.

Mutual funds accounted for 61 per cent of the anchor book.

Global institutional investors, including Norway's Government Pension Fund Global and asset manager Schroders, also participated in the anchor allocation, alongside domestic investment firms such as Carnelian, 360 ONE, Unifi and Nuvama.

The public issue will open on October 26 and close on October 28. The company has fixed a price band of ₹1,585-1,665 per share, valuing it at ₹10,765 crore at the upper end.

The IPO is entirely an Offer for Sale (OFS) by the Edelweiss Group, with no fresh issue component. Consequently, EAAA India Alternatives will not receive any proceeds from the offering; the selling shareholder will receive the entire amount.

The issue size has been reduced to ₹1,200 crore from the ₹1,500 crore proposed in the draft red herring prospectus filed with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in January.

Shares are expected to list on the BSE and NSE on November 2.

Incorporated in 2008, EAAA India Alternatives is an alternative investment platform managing long-term capital across asset classes, including infrastructure, commercial real estate and private credit. The company operates across Mumbai, New Delhi, GIFT City and Singapore.

data.title: Zymeworks Presents New Phase 1 Data for Folate Receptor Alpha-Targeting Antibody-Drug Conjugate ZW191 at ESMO Congress 2026
data.description:
Key points:
  • ZW191 demonstrates compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer across folate receptor alpha (FRα) expression levels
  • Confirmed objective response rates (cORR) of 64.5% at the 6.4 mg/kg dose in patients with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer
  • Median duration of response not yet reached at either dose level at median 7 months follow-up, with six-month progression-free survival rate of 61% in both groups
  • Favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, supports continued clinical development in partnership or through a strategic collaboration
  • Conference call with Zymeworks management on October 27 at 8:30 am Eastern Time (ET)

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zymeworks Inc. , a biotechnology company managing a portfolio of licensed healthcare assets while developing a diverse pipeline of novel, multifunctional biotherapeutics, today presented new clinical data from the randomized dose-optimization portion of its ongoing Phase 1 study evaluating ZW191, a FRα-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 in Madrid, Spain.

The presentation highlights compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC), including patients with high-grade serous disease across all levels of FRα expression. The results demonstrate compelling response rates, durability and a favorable tolerability profile, particularly at the 6.4 mg/kg dose, further supporting the potential of ZW191 to address limitations of currently available FRα-targeted therapies and expand treatment opportunities for patients with ovarian cancer.

“We are highly encouraged by these results, which further demonstrate the differentiated clinical profile of ZW191 and its potential to deliver meaningful benefit to patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer,” said Sabeen Mekan, M.D., Senior Vice President and Chief Medical Officer, Zymeworks. “The robust response rates observed at both doses, including meaningful activity in patients with low or negative FRα expression, reinforce the potential of ZW191 to benefit a broader patient population. Importantly, the encouraging durability of responses and favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, provide valuable insights to guide dose selection and the next stage of clinical development.”

The analysis included efficacy and safety data from 80 patients with PROC randomized to receive ZW191 at 6.4 mg/kg (n=37) or 9.6 mg/kg (n=43) every three weeks, as of the September 10, 2026 data cutoff date. Patients were heavily pretreated, having received a median of four prior lines of therapy, with 45% receiving five or more prior lines. Median follow-up was seven months. FRα expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry and categorized as low/negative (0%–24%), intermediate (25%–74%) or high (75%–100%) based on the percentage of tumor cells with 2+ or 3+ staining intensity.

Key Findings

Among response-evaluable patients with high-grade serous PROC, ZW191 demonstrated a cORR of 64.5% at 6.4 mg/kg and 55.3% at 9.6 mg/kg, with disease control rates of 100% and 92.1%, respectively. These findings demonstrate compelling anti-tumor activity at both doses in a heavily pretreated patient population.

ZW191 demonstrated meaningful anti-tumor activity across FRα expression in patients with high-grade serous PROC. Confirmed objective response rates were 69.2% in patients with high FRα expression, 50.0% in patients with intermediate FRα expression and 55.0% in patients with low or negative FRα expression. These findings support the potential of ZW191 to show improved efficacy than existing FRα targeted therapies in FRα high population and meaningfully benefit patients with lower expression who may not be eligible for currently approved FRα targeting therapies.

Responses to ZW191 were deep and durable, with median duration of response not yet reached at either dose. Six-month progression-free survival (PFS) was 61% in both groups, while median PFS was 7.9 months at 6.4 mg/kg and 9.8 months at 9.6 mg/kg in patients with high-grade serous PROC. At the time of data cutoff, 45% of patients remained on treatment, and PFS data continue to mature, especially at 6.4 mg/kg.

ZW191 continued to demonstrate a favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 22% of patients receiving 6.4 mg/kg compared with 44% at 9.6 mg/kg. Treatment-emergent adverse events leading to dose reductions occurred in 5% and 33% of patients, respectively, while discontinuations due to adverse events occurred in 14% and 19%. No deaths due to treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in either treatment group. The overall safety profile was manageable and supports continued clinical development.

“These results are particularly promising for patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer who have exhausted available treatment options,” said Jung-Yun Lee, M.D., Ph.D., Yonsei Cancer Center and Severance Hospital, Seoul, Republic of South Korea, and primary investigator who presented the results at ESMO 2026. “We observed substantial anti-tumor activity in patients who had received multiple prior therapies, including meaningful responses across high, intermediate and low or negative FRα expression levels. The encouraging durability of responses, together with the favorable safety profile observed at the lower dose, suggests ZW191 has the potential to become an important new treatment option for patients with this difficult-to-treat disease.”

The findings demonstrate encouraging anti-tumor activity across the 6.4 mg/kg and 9.6 mg/kg dose levels, with a more favorable tolerability profile at 6.4 mg/kg. These results will inform optimal dose selection for further clinical development.

ZW191's differentiated profile, including its novel FRα-targeting antibody, proprietary topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, ZD06519, and high drug-to-antibody ratio, supports its potential to address key limitations of existing therapies and broaden the applicability of FRα-targeted treatment approaches.

The presentation will be available on Zymeworks’ website at www.zymeworks.com/publications/.

Investor Call Details

Zymeworks invites investors and the general public to view and listen to a live webcast of its conference call with investment analysts at 8:30 am ET on October 27, 2026.

Dial-in details and webcast link are available on Zymeworks’ website at https://ir.zymeworks.com/events-and-presentations. A webcast replay of the call will be available on the Zymeworks website within 24 hours following the conclusion of the live call and will be archived for a limited period.

About ZW191

ZW191 is an antibody-drug conjugate engineered to target a protein called folate receptor-⍺ found in ~75% of high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas,1 over 50% of endometrial cancers,2,3 and ~70% of lung adenocarcinomas4. ZW191’s differentiated design strongly supports its ability to internalize into FR⍺-expressing cells with the potential to release bystander active topoisomerase-1 inhibitor (ZD06519), a novel proprietary payload developed by Zymeworks to kill tumor cells.

The Company has engaged MTS Healthcare to evaluate strategic partnering opportunities to fund further development for ZW191 with the objective of maximizing long-term value.

About Zymeworks Inc.

Zymeworks is a global biotechnology company building a diversified portfolio of healthcare assets designed to generate durable cash flows while advancing innovative medicines for difficult-to-treat diseases. The Company’s asset and royalty aggregation strategy combines a growing portfolio of commercial and near-commercial assets, including YUPELRI® (revefenacin), with a differentiated internal research and development engine. Zymeworks’ portfolio also includes Ziihera® (zanidatamab-hrii), a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody discovered and developed by Zymeworks and commercialized through global partnerships with Jazz Pharmaceuticals and BeOne Medicines, and pasritamig, a clinical-stage multispecific antibody developed by Johnson & Johnson using Zymeworks’ proprietary antibody engineering technologies.

Zymeworks is advancing a diverse pipeline of novel biotherapeutics, leveraging its proprietary Azymetric™ platform and expertise in antibody-drug conjugates, multispecific antibodies and other next-generation antibody technologies. These capabilities, together with Zymeworks’ integrated drug development expertise, enable the Company to develop differentiated therapeutics and create value through both internal innovation and strategic partnerships.

data.title: Immatics Presents Clinical Activity of IMA402 PRAME Bispecific and IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy across Advanced Solid Tumors in Two Oral Presentations at 2026 ESMO Annual Meeting
data.description:
Key points:
  • IMA402 PRAME bispecific continues to demonstrate encouraging anti-tumor activity in multiple indications, alongside a favorable safety profile
  • IMA402 achieved a cORR of 32%, 12.5 months median DOR and a 1-year OS rate of 91% in advanced melanoma patients with high PRAME expression
  • Clinical profile of IMA402 reinforces development path across multiple solid tumor indications, including melanoma, gynecologic cancers and lung cancer, in earlier and later treatment lines, supported by Immatics’ innovative, rapid liquid biopsy-based PRAME testing
  • IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy demonstrated deep and durable anti-tumor activity across multiple tumor types with a manageable safety profile, supporting its tumor-agnostic potential. At clinically relevant dose levels in patients with advanced, heavily pretreated gynecologic cancers, cORR was 55% with a median DOR of 8.4 months

Houston, Texas and Tuebingen, Germany, October 24, 2026 – Immatics N.V. (NASDAQ: IMTX, “Immatics” or the “Company”), the global leader in precision targeting of PRAME with multiple clinical-stage programs spanning cell therapies and bispecifics, today announced updated clinical trial data from its ongoing Phase 1b study with IMA402 PRAME bispecific and its Phase 1 study with IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy.

The IMA402 data will be presented in a rapid oral presentation (1955RO) by Dirk Schadendorf, M.D., and the IMA203CD8 data were presented in an oral presentation (1946O) by Antonia Busse, M.D., at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) in Madrid, Spain. In addition, exploratory analyses of the anzu-cel Phase 1b melanoma cohort will be presented in a poster (2128P) by Sapna Patel, M.D. The slides are available in the ‘Events & Presentations’ section of the Investor & Media page on the Company’s website.

“The data presented at ESMO further underscore the potential of IMA402 as an off-the-shelf treatment option for patients with solid cancers. This promising clinical profile reinforces our strategy as we continue to advance IMA402 across multiple cancer types and treatment lines, with combination approaches further expanding its reach,” said Cedrik Britten, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer at Immatics. “In addition, as the IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy data continue to mature, we are increasingly encouraged by its broad potential for patients with advanced PRAME-positive cancers. Together with anzu-cel, IMA402 and IMA203CD8 give us three distinct and complementary approaches to target PRAME, with the potential to reach more patients across a broad range of cancers.”

Rapid Oral Presentation Summary - IMA402 PRAME TCR Bispecific Phase 1b Trial

Patient Population: Heavily pretreated patient population with a median of 3 prior lines of therapy

As of the data cutoff on June 1, 2026, 126 heavily pretreated patients across multiple tumor types, primarily melanoma and ovarian cancer, received at least one infusion of IMA402 during the dose escalation or dose expansion part of the ongoing trial (NCT05958121). Patients had received a median of 3 prior lines of systemic treatment, had a median target lesion sum of diameter of 7.4 cm and had a median of 4 tumor lesions. The efficacy population included 40 patients treated within the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) range of 10 to 45 mg across varying levels of PRAME expression. Within this population, 31 patients exhibited high PRAME expression levels (PRAME-high)1 in their tumors. Of these, all patients with PRAME-high melanoma had received prior systemic treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), with a median of 2 prior ICI regimens and all patients with PRAME-high ovarian cancer were previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy.

Safety: Favorable tolerability profile as monotherapy and as combination therapy

IMA402 showed favorable tolerability across all doses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were expected, transient lymphopenia and low-grade cytokine release syndrome (CRS), consistent with the mechanism of action. No cases of ICANS were reported. No IMA402-related Grade 5 events were reported. Tolerability was consistent across all evaluated doses, including the RP2D range, with no additive toxicity observed when combined with an ICI.

Anti-tumor Activity and Durability: 32% cORR in PRAME-high melanoma with promising durability and survivalIMA402 showed promising anti-tumor activity as monotherapy (n=36) or in combination with an immune checkpoint inhibitor (n=4) in the efficacy population at RP2D range. Treatment with IMA402 demonstrated 10 confirmed responses resulting in an overall confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 25% (10/40) and a disease control rate (DCR) of 63% (25/40). This includes one confirmed complete response in melanoma. The longest ongoing response exceeded 2 years. In the PRAME-high population, cORR was 32% (10/31) across all indications and 32% (7/22) in patients with melanoma. The PRAME-high melanoma population further showed a median duration of response (mDOR) of 12.5 months (median follow-up, mFU, 16.8 months). Median overall survival (mOS) was not reached (mFU 8.8 months), with 91% of patients alive at 1 year (versus 60% of patients treated below RP2D range), indicating promising overall survival data irrespective of best response. Among 6 patients with PRAME-high ovarian cancer, 3 confirmed responses were reported.

Next Development Steps for IMA402:

The promising clinical profile of IMA402 supports a development path across various solid tumors in earlier and later treatment lines. These include combination approaches with ICIs in melanoma and in gynecologic cancers as well as IMA402 in combination with the Company’s MAGEA4/8-directed bispecific, IMA401, in lung cancer with first data expected in 2027. Furthermore, the use of Immatics’ proprietary rapid, sensitive and reliable liquid biopsy-based PRAME testing enables precise patient selection and could support potential fast-to-market strategies, subject to regulatory approval, in PRAME-high melanoma and beyond.

Oral Presentation Summary - IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy Phase 1 Trial

Patient population: Heavily pretreated patient population with limited treatment options

As of the data cutoff on August 7, 2026, 98 heavily pretreated patients across multiple advanced solid tumor types expressing PRAME that had undergone a median of 3 prior systemic treatments were enrolled in the ongoing Phase 1 dose escalation/dose expansion trial (NCT03686124). Of these, 90 patients were evaluable for efficacy, including 27 with gynecologic cancers (ovarian and uterine cancer), 44 with melanoma, 12 with synovial sarcoma and 7 with other solid tumor types. All patients with ovarian cancer had received prior platinum-based therapy.

Safety: Treatment with IMA203CD8 was manageable

IMA203CD8 demonstrated a consistent and manageable safety profile across different solid tumor types and a wide dose range (median dose 1.81x109 TCR T cells, range 0.44-12.50x109). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were expected and included transient cytopenias associated with the lymphodepletion regimen and low-grade cytokine release syndrome (CRS), consistent with the mechanism of action. ICANS was infrequently observed, and no IMA203CD8-related Grade 5 events occurred. Maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was not reached with doses up to 12.5 billion IMA203CD8 cells.

Anti-tumor Activity and Durability: One-time infusion of IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy showed anti-tumor activity across multiple tumor types

Across all evaluated dose levels and tumor types, including lower dose levels not selected for further clinical development, a one-time infusion of IMA203CD8 demonstrated an ORR of 51% (46/90) and a cORR of 41% (36/87). The DCR was 82% (74/90) and 83% (71/86) of patients with evaluable target lesions experienced tumor reduction. Responses were observed across multiple solid tumors expressing PRAME, including ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, melanoma, synovial sarcoma, and others. Durable long-term responses were observed with ongoing responses for more than 2.5 years.

Next Development Steps for IMA203CD8:

Phase 1a dose escalation is complete. Immatics is currently enrolling patients with uterine cancer at clinically relevant doses to further expand the clinical dataset in this indication. In addition, a Phase 1/2 investigator-initiated trial (IIT) in patients with PRAME-positive pediatric cancers is planned to start in 1H 2027. The clinical activity of IMA203CD8 observed across tumor types with distinct biology and differing levels of PRAME expression, including ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, melanoma and synovial sarcoma, supports the broad applicability of IMA203CD8 across PRAME-positive cancers. The development approach for IMA203CD8 will leverage targeted cohorts of selected tumor types, such as ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, rare cancers and pediatric cancers to build the clinical evidence base for broader, tumor-agnostic application.

Poster Presentation Summary – Anzu-cel Phase 1b Melanoma Cohort

Additional exploratory analyses (data cutoff Sept 24, 2025) of anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel, IMA203), presented in a poster (2128P) by Sapna Patel, M.D., demonstrated durable clinical benefit following a one-time treatment in a heavily pretreated population of patients with advanced melanoma. Durable clinical benefit was observed across patients with varied baseline clinical and treatment characteristics, with no single characteristic identified as a predictor of prolonged PFS. Exploratory analyses suggested that lower tumor burden, lower LDH, and a higher effector-to-target ratio may be associated with longer PFS. These findings further strengthen the clinical profile of anzu-cel, which is currently being evaluated in the Phase 3 SUPRAME trial in advanced melanoma.

About IMA402 PRAME Bispecific

IMA402 is a molecule from Immatics’ TCR bispecifics (TCER®) pipeline directed against an HLA-A*02:01-presented peptide derived from PRAME. IMA402 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1b clinical trial in patients with solid tumors expressing PRAME. IMA402 is part of Immatics’ strategy to leverage the full clinical potential of targeting PRAME, one of the most promising targets for TCR-based therapies.

About IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy

IMA203CD8 is Immatics’ PRAME-directed TCR T-cell therapy engineered to recognize an intracellular PRAME-derived peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on the cell surface and initiate a potent and specific anti-tumor response. Co-transduction of CD8αβ with the PRAME TCR adds functional CD4+ T cells designed to boost anti-tumor activity. IMA203CD8 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1b clinical trial in solid tumors expressing PRAME.

About Anzu-cel PRAME Cell Therapy

Anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel; IMA203) is a PRAME-directed TCR T-cell therapy engineered to recognize an intracellular PRAME-derived peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on the cell surface and initiate a potent and specific anti-tumor response. Anzu-cel PRAME cell therapy is currently being evaluated in a registration-enabling randomized controlled Phase 3 trial, “SUPRAME,” in patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma who have disease progression on or after treatment with at least one checkpoint inhibitor. In parallel, the Phase 1/2 clinical trial is ongoing with a focus on uveal melanoma.

About PRAME

PRAME is a tumor-associated target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Immatics’ PRAME franchise includes multiple product candidates, therapeutic modalities, indications and combination approaches: anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel; IMA203) and IMA203CD8, both PRAME-directed cell therapies, and IMA402, a PRAME-directed bispecific. Combination approaches include IMA402 with immune checkpoint inhibitors, IMA402 with the MAGEA4/8-directed bispecific IMA401, and anzu-cel in combination with Moderna’s PRAME mRNA therapy designed to enhance the cell therapy response.

Immatics is committed to making a meaningful impact on the lives of patients with cancer. We are the global leader in precision targeting of PRAME, a target expressed in more than 50 cancers. data.title: S&P set to change how it classifies US growth and value stocks
data.description:
S&P Dow Jones Indices is changing how it classifies US stocks as growth or value, dropping share price momentum from its growth assessment and adding free cash flow to its value assessment.

The changes will affect indices such as the S&P 500 Growth and S&P 500 Value, along with corresponding indices tracking mid-cap and small-cap stocks. According to an S&P Dow Jones Indices release dated October 23, the revised rules will take effect on December 21, 2026, as part of its annual index reconstitution.

Under the current rules, S&P Dow Jones Indices assesses growth stocks using three factors: the change in earnings per share over three years relative to the current share price, three-year sales per share growth and share price momentum over 12 months.

Under the new rules, it will drop the momentum factor and use the other two measures to assess growth stocks.

The changes to the value framework are more extensive. S&P Dow Jones Indices will replace the traditional book value-to-price ratio with an adjusted measure that accounts for intangible assets.

Changes to S&P's growth and value factors

It will also combine trailing earnings-to-price with forward one-year earnings-to-price, using a simple average of the two. The sales-to-price ratio will remain, while free cash flow-to-price will be added as a new factor.

Free cash flow is the cash a company generates after accounting for capital spending. By adding this measure, the index provider will use another way to assess a company's value relative to its share price. However, the new free cash flow measure will not apply to real estate, banks, insurance and certain financial services industries. These sectors and industries will be assessed using the other value factors.

Clients will first see the changes in preliminary index files from December 4, before the revised indices take effect ahead of the market opening on December 21.

data.title: Darolutamide plus ADT and radiation therapy reduces risk of metastasis or death by 58% in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence
data.description:
ORION CORPORATION

PRESS RELEASE

24 OCTOBER 2026 at 9.35 EEST

Darolutamide plus ADT and radiation therapy reduces risk of metastasis or death by 58% in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence

  • Interim analysis results from the Phase 3 trial DASL-HiCaP show a 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death in the combined primary endpoint of metastasis-free survival (MFS-CI) with darolutamide versus placebo, in addition to androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and radiation therapy
  • Four-year metastasis-free survival rate in trial reached 95% with darolutamide compared to 88% with placebo, alongside secondary endpoint improvements and a safety profile consistent with previous studies
  • Results will be presented as a late-breaking abstract in a Presidential Symposium at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026

ESPOO, Finland, October 24, 2026 – New late-breaking data to be presented today at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 will show that adding darolutamide, an androgen receptor inhibitor (ARi) initially discovered by Orion Pharma, to standard-of-care androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and locoregional radiation therapy (RT), significantly improves metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI) in prostate cancer patients with high risk of recurrence compared to placebo. Darolutamide is currently not approved for this treatment setting. These data will be presented at Presidential Symposium I at the ESMO Congress 2026 (LBA4, Saturday 24 October, 16:30 CET).

At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the interim analysis demonstrated a 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death with darolutamide plus ADT and RT compared with placebo plus ADT and RT (hazard ratio [HR] 0.42; 95% CI: 0.27–0.66; p=0.0001). The 4-year metastasis-free survival rate was 95% for patients receiving darolutamide compared with 88% for those receiving placebo.

Secondary endpoints also showed consistent positive trends with darolutamide, with a 53% reduction in the risk of prostate-specific antigen progression free survival (PSA-PFS; HR 0.47; 95% CI: 0.33–0.67), and a 4-year PSA-PFS rate of 91% versus 83% with placebo. Prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS) and overall survival (OS) hazard ratios were 0.58 (95% CI: 0.17–1.97; 99% vs 99% at 4 years) and 0.88 (95% CI: 0.49–1.59; 97% vs 95% at 4 years), respectively, with follow-up ongoing.

The safety profile of darolutamide was consistent with its known tolerability, with adverse events being similar to the placebo group. Proportions of patients experiencing Grade ≥2 adverse events of special interest for darolutamide versus placebo were: fatigue/asthenia (14% vs 10%), hypertension (7% vs 9%), fractures (2% vs 3%), and cardiac events (3% vs 3%). Any Grade ≥3 adverse event occurred in 43% of patients in the darolutamide group versus 36% in the placebo group.

Follow-up of participants is continuing to provide further information on longer-term outcomes, including overall survival.

About the DASL-HiCaP trial (ANZUP1801)

The DASL-HiCaP trial is an investigator-initiated, randomized, placebo-controlled, Phase III trial (NCT04136353) evaluating darolutamide added to standard-of-care ADT and locoregional radiation therapy in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence. DASL-HiCaP is conducted by the University of Sydney and ANZUP Clinical Trials Group and is the fourth Phase III trial for darolutamide. Following ARAMIS, ARASENS, and ARANOTE, which demonstrated darolutamide’s efficacy and safety in advanced prostate cancer, DASL-HiCaP represents the first Phase III study of darolutamide in early prostate cancer. A total of 1,106 participants across Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United States, Ireland and the United Kingdom were randomized 1:1 to receive darolutamide (600 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 96 weeks, combined with an LHRH analog for 96 weeks and RT to the prostate/prostate bed and pelvic lymph nodes. The primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS CI). Secondary endpoints included prostate-specific antigen progression free survival (PSA-PFS), prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS), and overall survival (OS). The protocol specified an interim analysis after 87 MFS-CI events; follow-up is ongoing to evaluate long-term overall survival.

About Prostate Cancer

Prostate cancer is the second most common cancer and the fourth most common cause of cancer death in men worldwide. Over 1.5 million men are diagnosed with prostate cancer each year and almost 420,000 die from the disease worldwide. By 2040, prostate cancer diagnoses are projected to increase to 2.9 million.

Standard therapy for prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence combines radiation therapy with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). However, despite this approach, a significant proportion of patients experience treatment failure, local recurrence, or distant metastases. Intensifying therapy early with an advanced androgen receptor inhibitor aims to improve long-term disease control and delay metastatic progression.

About darolutamide (Nubeqa™)

Darolutamide is an oral ARi with a unique chemical structure that binds with high affinity to the androgen receptor and exhibits a strong antagonistic effect against the androgen receptor inhibiting the receptor function and growth of prostate cancer cells. Additionally, preclinical models and neuroimaging data in healthy humans, support darolutamide's low potential for blood-brain barrier penetration and low potential for clinically relevant drug drug interactions.

Darolutamide, under the brand name Nubeqa™ plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), is already approved in more than 85 markets around the world, including the US, EU and China. It is approved for the treatment of adult patients with mHSPC without docetaxel in 75 markets and with docetaxel in more than 85 countries, and for adult patients with nmCRPC at high risk of developing metastatic disease in more than 85 countries.

Darolutamide is developed jointly by Orion Pharma and Bayer.

A robust clinical development program is underway investigating darolutamide across various stages of prostate cancer. Current ongoing trials include the Phase III ARASTEP trial evaluating the efficacy of darolutamide plus ADT compared to ADT alone in hormone sensitive prostate cancer (HSPC), in patients with high-risk biochemical recurrence (BCR) who have no evidence of metastatic disease by conventional imaging and a positive PSMA PET/CT at baseline.

data.title: Firstwork Raises $15 Mn In Series A Round Led By Earlybird Venture Capital
data.description:
US-based HR tech startup plans to expand its AI-led workforce automation platform across the US and Europe, with 80 per cent of its workforce based in Bengaluru

US-based HR technology startup Firstwork has raised USD 15 million (over Rs 142 crore) in a Series A funding round led by Earlybird Venture Capital to expand its AI-powered workforce automation platform across the US and Europe, as per a media report.

The round also saw participation from Legion VC and Deel Ventures, alongside existing investors Gradient and Y Combinator. The latest fundraise takes Firstwork’s total funding to USD 20 million since its launch in 2024.

The San Francisco-based startup plans to use the capital to expand its teams across applied AI, AI research, engineering and go-to-market functions. Around 80 per cent of its workforce operates from Bengaluru. The company also plans to strengthen its presence in the US and Europe and extend its AI agents to additional workforce operations.

Founded by former Deel executives Vardhan Kapoor and Shubham Choudhary, Firstwork uses AI agents to automate human resource operations for frontline workers. Its platform covers document verification, background checks, right-to-work checks, onboarding, training coordination, compliance management and worker follow-ups.

The platform integrates with existing HR systems, allowing employers to automate workflows without replacing their current software.

According to the company, more than 1.5 lakh frontline workers start work through its platform every month. Firstwork claims its technology can reduce the time spent by workers and HR teams on each new hire by up to 90 per cent. Its clients include Deel, Job&Talent, Relay, Wonolo and BGSF.

The fundraise comes amid increasing adoption of artificial intelligence across human resource functions. India's HR technology market is projected to grow to USD 2.3 billion by 2033 from USD 1.12 billion in 2024, according to industry estimates.

Several Indian startups are developing AI-based solutions for recruitment, onboarding and workforce management. Bengaluru-based Hunar.AI, which raised Rs 40 crore earlier this week, uses conversational AI agents to automate gig-worker hiring, onboarding, training and employee retention. Its clients include Swiggy, Zepto, Croma, Starbucks and Dr Lal PathLabs.

Hyderabad-based TurboHire raised USD 6 million in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures in August 2025 to expand its agentic AI-based recruitment platform. Founded in 2019, the startup automates enterprise hiring workflows and says it has onboarded more than 120 enterprises, including Cipla, Tata Motors, PwC, Lenskart and Britannia.

Other companies operating in adjacent segments include TraqCheck, which offers AI-powered background verification and recruitment agents, and HireBound, which automates candidate sourcing, screening and evaluation.

data.title: IDBI Bank Unions Back Nationwide Strike Against Stake Sale
data.description:
UFBU backs the November 2–3 protest over the proposed Fairfax deal, citing concerns over public ownership and employee safeguards

IDBI Bank employees are set to stage a two-day nationwide strike on November 2 and 3, opposing the proposed sale of the bank to Canadian investor Fairfax Financial Holdings, with the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) extending support to the agitation.

In a circular dated October 22, the UFBU urged its affiliated unions and members to participate in solidarity programmes, backing the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees’ campaign against the proposed sale of a 60% stake held by the government and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC).

The UFBU has questioned the proposed transfer of ownership and management control to a foreign investor, arguing that it raises concerns over the bank’s public-sector character. It has also cited a parliamentary assurance made in 2003 that the government would retain at least a 51% stake in IDBI.

The employee forum has demanded that the government halt the transaction and acquire an additional 6% equity in the bank, either from LIC or through market purchases, to maintain majority ownership. It has also sought written assurances that existing service conditions, welfare measures, pension benefits and reservation policies will be protected, along with the continuation of industry-level wage revisions.

As part of its solidarity campaign, the UFBU has called for participation in demonstrations and a social media campaign, besides other protest activities ahead of the strike.

The proposed agitation comes as the government moves to divest its stake in IDBI Bank, a lender that the unions say has returned to profitability in recent years. The strike is intended to press for a reconsideration of the proposed transaction and safeguards for employees.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Says Refiners See 'High Probability' Of Sharp Oil Supply Drop As Houthi Attacks Escalate — Crude Oil Prices Hit 6-Month High
data.description:
Key points:
  • According to Struyven, refiners are among those buying more crude because of the intensification of shipping attacks and strikes on infrastructure by the Houthis.
  • Crude oil prices rose to a six-month high, with the U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures expiring in December rising 4.46% to $103.44 a barrel after a 7.81% gain the week before.
  • Brent crude futures expiring in December rose 6.24% this week, hovering around $116.93 a barrel after a 4.91% increase the week before.

Crude oil prices have climbed to a six-month high as escalating attacks and rising tensions in the Middle East add to concerns about energy supply disruptions.

The latest escalation comes as fighting involving the Iran-aligned Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition has intensified, while shipping incidents have added to concerns around key waterways used to transport oil.

Goldman Sachs' co-head of Global Commodities Research and head of Oil Research, Daan Struyven, said the recent rise in crude prices reflects growing downside risks to supply, with physical buyers and investors both contributing to the stronger market.

Crude Oil Prices Hit Six-Month High

Crude oil prices rose to a six-month high, with the U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures expiring in December rising 4.46% to $103.44 a barrel after a 7.81% gain the week before. Brent crude futures expiring in December rose 6.24% this week, hovering around $116.93 a barrel after a 4.91% increase the week before.

The United States Oil Fund ETF (USO) rose more than 4% on Friday, while the ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil ETF (UCO) gained about 4%.

Goldman Sachs Sees Growing Downside Risks To Oil Supply

Struyven said Brent crude had risen sharply as growing Middle East tensions and increasing downside risks to supply prompted buyers to bid up barrels in both physical and financial markets.

According to Struyven, refiners are among those buying more crude because of the intensification of shipping attacks and strikes on infrastructure by the Houthis. With inventories low, physical buyers are trying to secure barrels while they remain available.

Struyven said refiners see a "high probability of a sharp drop in supply," helping explain the precautionary buying taking place in the physical oil market.

He also pointed to financial-market demand, saying investors are buying oil as a hedge against higher energy prices because bonds and equities have become unusually sensitive to movements in crude.

Goldman Sachs sees the risks to oil prices as increasingly symmetrical following the recent surge, although Struyven said risks to the firm's forecasts remain skewed to the upside.

The bank's base case calls for Brent to end this year at $90 a barrel and average $80 a barrel in 2027. Struyven identified an intensification of shipping attacks, damage to oil infrastructure and a more persistent risk premium as key upside risks.

The analyst highlighted that crude oil exports from the Persian Gulf had reached about 110% of 2025 average levels over the previous couple of weeks, while refined-product exports such as diesel were running at only about 40% of the 2025 average.

He attributed part of the disparity to damage to refineries in the Middle East and the greater difficulty of arranging ship-to-ship transfers for refined products.

Goldman Sachs also sees factors beyond the Middle East supporting refined-product prices. Struyven pointed to structural tightness stemming from years of underinvestment, as well as reduced diesel production at Russian refineries following Ukrainian drone attacks.

Houthi Attacks Add To Middle East Supply Concerns

Tensions around key Middle East shipping routes have intensified in recent weeks, with attacks involving the Iran-aligned Houthis adding to concerns over the movement of oil and other energy products.

According to a Reuters report, Saudi Aramco ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran on Thursday, as fighting intensified between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. Dhahran is located near Bahrain and is home to the headquarters of the world's largest crude oil exporter.

Separately, an oil spill was detected off the coast of Umm Al Quwain in the United Arab Emirates, according to the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment. The ministry did not say what caused the spill, and authorities had not identified the tanker involved.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, rose 0.15%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) edged up by 0.07%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) gained 0.13%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘extremely bearish’ territory at the time of writing.
